result.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
result.comment: Project page at https://xiaofengshi.github.io/InstructReplay/ and code at https://github.com/xiaofengShi/InstructReplay
result.summary: Fine-tuning an instruction-tuned language model on new facts often erodes its general abilities. We find that standard fine-tuning lowers instruction-following, reasoning and coding benchmarks by 35 points on average, and that these losses track a collapse in answer length: fine-tuned models at least halve their responses, and the further a response drifts from the initial model's length, the more often it fails. We propose InstructReplay: the initial model answers a set of general instructions once, and during fine-tuning the model is kept close to the initial model on these answers. Across three model families and two domains, InstructReplay reduces the average decline on five general benchmarks from 28.1 to 2.4 points and keeps answer length close to the initial model's, while learning the new facts as well as standard fine-tuning. It balances learning and retention better than seven adaptation methods in all six settings. Controlled comparisons attribute the gain to replaying the model's own answers to general instructions rather than to the form of the loss.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现用新事实微调指令模型会显著损害通用能力，且这种退化与回答长度骤减同步出现；提出 InstructReplay，先在通用指令上采集初始模型自身的回答，再在微调时约束模型靠近这些回答，从而兼顾新事实学习与能力保持。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「回放自身回答＋对初始模型做正则」的思路可能为 LVR 微调中保留推理轨迹形态、抑制推理长度与行为坍缩提供可核查的借鉴；但论文为纯文本事实微调，未涉及视觉或多模态 latent 状态。
